title: IT Act Section 43 / 66 — Unauthorized Access
summary: Scripts that install tracking cookies or access device data without consent fall under unauthorized access/data theft provisions. This targets the site operator, not a user who was tricked into clicking.

title: Don't click inside the ad at all
summary: Close via the browser tab or window control, not the ad's own 'X' — fake close buttons can still trigger scripts. Keep a pop-up blocker enabled.

title: If you already clicked
summary: Close the tab without clicking anything else. Turn off Wi-Fi or switch to airplane mode to stop any script from reaching a remote server. Run a full security scan afterward. If you entered any personal info, contact your bank.

title: Streaming vs. downloading — a real legal distinction
summary: The Bombay High Court has clarified that simply viewing/streaming pirated content for personal use, without downloading or sharing, is not treated as a criminal offense for the viewer. The liability falls mainly on the sites hosting and distributing the content.

title: Copyright Act, 1957 — Sections 63, 65A, 65B
summary: Downloading, copying, or distributing pirated content is punishable — up to 3 years imprisonment (7 for repeat/large-scale offenses) and fines from roughly ₹50,000 upward, depending on severity.

title: Never grant notification permissions to unfamiliar sites
summary: Once granted, a site can keep pushing ads and redirect links even after you've closed the browser. Treat any 'Allow notifications to continue' prompt on a streaming site as a red flag, not a requirement.

title: If you granted notification access or hit a redirect chain
summary: Revoke the permission immediately: browser settings → site settings → notifications → remove. Don't follow any further redirects. If a page asked for payment or personal info, treat it like a phishing incident.

title: IT Act Section 66C — Identity Theft
summary: Fraudulent or dishonest use of passwords, electronic signatures, or other unique identifiers — including stolen OTPs — is a specific, punishable offense under this section.

title: IT Act Section 66D — Cheating by Personation
summary: Covers cheating by impersonation using a computer resource — directly applicable to apps or actors that use stolen OTPs/credentials to access accounts.

title: Only install from the Play Store, and read permissions
summary: A streaming app never legitimately needs SMS access or Accessibility Service. Accessibility Service specifically can let an app read your screen and simulate taps — this is the mechanism behind OTP theft. Keep 'install from unknown sources' disabled.

title: If you already installed one
summary: Turn off Wi-Fi/mobile data immediately. Contact your bank to freeze the card and watch for unauthorized charges. Uninstall the app after revoking its Accessibility Service access in Settings first.

title: Report it — official channel
summary: Call the national cybercrime helpline at 1930, or file a report at cybercrime.gov.in. This is the correct first step for any of the three scenarios if real harm may have occurred — don't panic, just report.
